subject.title: fix: discord exec approvals fails against local self-signed TLS gateway

question: Should maintainers repair and land the active shared-bootstrap TLS fingerprint PR, or replace it with a clean equivalent fix?
rationale: The issue changes Gateway TLS trust decisions for approval/bootstrap clients, and the active candidate is open but conflicting with prior review concerns, so a maintainer should choose the repair path before more automation opens another fix.

options.title: Repair active PR
options.body: Use the open shared-bootstrap PR as the candidate, fix its current-main drift and import blocker, then rerun focused Gateway/ACP/MCP validation.

options.title: Replace with clean PR
options.body: Set the active branch aside and land a new narrow shared-bootstrap repair that preserves the same TLS target-selection semantics.

options.title: Hold for TLS policy review
options.body: Keep the issue open without landing until maintainers revisit local, remote, CLI, and env TLS pin precedence as a broader trust-policy decision.

recommendation.title: Repair active PR
recommendation.body: Use the open shared-bootstrap PR as the candidate, fix its current-main drift and import blocker, then rerun focused Gateway/ACP/MCP validation.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest feature-history trail for shared Gateway approval/bootstrap and TLS trust-boundary decisions points to this owner.
